stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Sweep both sliders and observe how the magnetic field around the straight wire responds to the current $I$ and the probe distance $r$. Advance when each slider has covered at least half its range.
stages.concept: The field around an infinite straight wire is $B = \mu_0 I / (2\pi r)$. The field lines are concentric circles around the wire. Doubling $I$ doubles $B$; doubling $r$ halves $B$. In SI units, this simplifies to $B[\mu\text{T}] = 20\,I / r$ when $I$ is in amperes and $r$ in centimetres.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: A target field magnitude $B^*$ is shown at the marked point M. Adjust the current $I$ and the probe distance $r$ until the field magnitude at your probe matches the target.
stages.concept: Many current-and-distance pairs produce the same $B$. The constraint is $\mu_0 I / (2\pi r) = B^*$, which has a one-parameter family of solutions — pick any $r$ then solve for $I$, or vice versa.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The field visualization is hidden. The target field magnitude $B^*$ at the point M is still shown. Compute a valid current and probe distance on paper, then set the sliders and submit. You have one attempt on this setup.
stages.concept: Rearrange the formula to $I = 2\pi r B^* / \mu_0$. Choose any probe distance $r$ within the slider range first, then compute the required $I$. Because $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}$, the algebra collapses to $I[\text{A}] = r[\text{cm}] \cdot B^*[\mu\text{T}] / 20$.

labels.tip1: sweep both sliders — watch the field lines brighten with I, weaken with r
labels.tip2: any (I, r) with mu0*I/(2*pi*r) = B* works — try r first, then solve I
labels.tip3: compute on paper: pick r, then I = r * B* / 20 (I in A, r in cm, B* in uT)
labels.peek_tip_formula: Rearrange: I = 2*pi*r*B / mu0. Pick any r, then compute I.
labels.peek_tip_anchor: Shortcut: I[A] = r[cm] * B[uT] / 20. For B=40uT at r=5cm, I=10A.

1.1: Slide the current I up and down while watching how the field lines around the wire brighten or fade.
1.2: Now sweep the probe distance r. Field lines closer to the wire are stronger — this is the 1/r falloff.
1.3: Keep going until each slider bar has visited both ends of its range (the coverage meter tracks this).

2.1: Read the target B* value on the marker M. The field at your probe must reach that magnitude.
2.2: Fix r at a convenient value (say 5 cm), then use B = mu0*I/(2*pi*r) to solve for the required I.
2.3: Direct shortcut in these units: I[A] = r[cm] * B*[uT] / 20. Try r=5cm, then I = 5 * B*/20.

3.1: The formula B = mu0*I/(2*pi*r) still holds — the visualization is only pedagogical scaffolding.
3.2: Rearrange for I: I = 2*pi*r*B*/mu0. Pick any r in the slider range, then compute I.
3.3: In classroom units: I[A] = r[cm] * B*[uT] / 20. Substitute your chosen r and the shown B* to get I directly.
